key: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
s: Among the ten words spoken at Sinai, this one opens the command on the seventh day; Rashi, on Exodus 20:8, takes ‘Remember’ as a charge to keep the day always in mind, setting aside for it any fine thing that comes to hand.

evidence.gloss: Remember: it is a verbal noun, without reference to time, like ‘eating and drinking’ (Isaiah 22) and ‘going and weeping’ (2 Samuel 3); and so its meaning is: set your heart to remember the sabbath day always, so that if a fine thing comes your way, you keep it ready for the sabbath (Mekhilta).

reason: verse.js ok true, ref Exodus 20:8 and at [69,8] match; the line itself names the sabbath, the text first under rule 8, and no gate warning of reuse. Plain sense: the verse opens the sabbath command (20:8 to 11) among the words God speaks at Sinai (Exodus 19 to 20; ‘the ten words’ is the Tanakh’s own term, Exodus 34:28): faithful, no words of the line repeated. The packet prints Rashi’s second comment on זכור in exactly the words quoted: remember the sabbath day always, so that a fine thing met in the week is kept for the sabbath. The sentence paraphrases this without drift; Rashi’s first comment (remember and observe in one utterance) is left aside, not contradicted. Hebrew public domain. entry-check ok with no warnings.
